role.altitude: The store investigator keeps spotting suspects, alerting staff and police, counting cash and judging shortages; working out expected cash and paging through till rolls for voids and refunds shrink.
skills_to_grow: Reading till exception reports without jumping to conclusions about staff
role.ambitious_version: An investigator who spots a pattern of refunds in a week instead of at the year-end stock count.

tasks.short: Spot or locate the suspect, alert appropriate personnel to the suspect's location by radio or phone, keep watching and updating, and log the alert.

steps.what: Investigator spots or locates the suspect
Investigator alerts security staff or police to the suspect's location by radio or phone
Investigator keeps the suspect in view and gives updates
Investigator logs the alert with times and outcome: in a paper incident log today, on a phone form that takes the alert time from the device after the change

tasks.design: Spotting, alerting and keeping watch stay fully with the investigator; no face recognition or behaviour analysis is used. The incident log is a phone form in the case register that takes the time of the alert from the device, so the investigator records only what happened.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incidents were written up on paper or in a spreadsheet afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: Case registers with mobile incident forms.
tasks.still_hard: Losing a suspect in a crowd.

reach.learn: Whether incident logs are complete and timely.

evidence.claim: The sector privacy code requires the least intrusive method and fixes dossier fields.
Untargeted face scraping and emotion recognition at work are banned under the AI Act.
Face matching in shops falls under an AI Act high-risk area; the design uses none.

assumptions: Boundary: alerting others about a located suspect; arrests are outside.
Input contract for s4: the investigator's entry on the phone form, with time taken from the device.
Spotting, alerting and watching keep their full time. s4 keeps 85 because only the alert time fills in and the investigator still writes what happened and the later times.
research_questions: Are incident logs used more in follow-up?

incremental.description: Investigator checks the logged times against the radio log.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the investigator often logs well after the alert, so the device time must be corrected (0.3); high: the alert is logged at the time (1.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count cash, compare it with the till's expected cash, review transactions, sales checks and register tapes for voids, refunds and no-sales to verify amounts or identify shortages, judge shortages and record findings.

steps.what: Investigator counts cash in the tills and the safe
Investigator compares the counted cash with the till's sales figures to verify amounts
Investigator reviews transactions on register tapes: voids, refunds, no-sales and discounts
Investigator judges whether shortages point to error or theft and decides follow-up
Investigator records the findings in the case register

tasks.design: The till system computes expected cash per drawer and shift, and the investigator enters the counted amount to see the difference at once. Fixed rules on the till's transaction log list exceptions, such as voids after payment, refunds without a receipt and frequent no-sales, by drawer and shift. Counting and judging whether a shortage is error or theft stay with the investigator. Because the lists can be read per cashier, the store's works council agrees the rules first, and staff are told the checks exist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Expected cash and exceptions were worked out from paper till rolls.
tasks.enabler_now: Till systems with cash reports and transaction logs that fixed rules can read.
tasks.still_hard: Telling a careless cashier from a dishonest one.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the store's habits before suspecting anyone.
tasks.altitude: Less paging through rolls; judging people stays human.

reach.learn: Whether exception lists show training needs rather than theft.

evidence.claim: Ledger and till queries for duplicate or odd entries are plain code.
Shop cameras and loss analytics also watch staff and need works council consent first.
The sector privacy code requires proportionality and telling the person investigated.

assumptions: Boundary: verifying cash and identifying shortages; interviews and dismissals are outside.
Input contract for s2: expected cash per drawer from the till system's cash report; the count entered by the investigator.
Input contract for s3: the till's transaction log with drawer, shift and cashier codes, on stores with networked tills (about 80%); others still use paper rolls; s3 is priced at that share.

Counting, judging and recording findings (a first record) keep their full time. s2 keeps 30 for entering the count and reading the difference; s3 keeps 50: 20 for stores with paper rolls and the rest for reading listed exceptions.
unknowns: Whether the works council agrees per-cashier exception lists.

already_counted.description: Investigator checks listed exceptions that turn out to be normal practice.

incremental.description: Investigator reviews the exception rules with the works council yearly.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only about half of the stores have networked tills, so more tapes are read by hand (24.0); high: about 80% networked as assumed (31.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
